worksheet.title: Break It Into Parts
worksheet.subtitle: Big things are made of small parts
worksheet.learning_goal: I can break a big picture into the small shapes that make it.

parts.title: Big things are made of parts
parts.text: Look closely and you will see that big things are built from smaller shapes. Breaking a big thing into its parts is called DECOMPOSITION.

parts.title: Watch Bit — a rocket is made of 2 parts
parts.note: Bit's rocket is a triangle on top of a square. That is 2 parts.

parts.title: A house — draw its 2 parts
parts.prompt: A house is made of a square ■ (walls) and a triangle ▲ (roof). Draw the two parts, one in each box.

parts.title: A snowman — draw its 3 parts
parts.prompt: A snowman is made of three circles ● ● ●. Draw the three parts, one in each box.

parts.title: You try — Bit the robot
parts.prompt: Bit is made of 4 parts: a square ■ body, a circle ● head, and two square ■ ■ feet. Draw all four parts, one in each box.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Breaking a big thing into small parts is called decomposition. Coders do it too — they break a big problem into small, easy steps.

teacher_guide.title: Break It Into Parts
teacher_guide.subtitle: Quick facilitation notes & answer key
teacher_guide.footer_topic: 6. Break It Into Parts — Teacher Guide

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children see that a whole picture is built from smaller shape parts, and name/draw those parts. Breaking a whole into parts is decomposition — the computational-thinking skill of splitting a big problem into smaller, manageable pieces.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children analyze how a whole is composed of parts.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child draws the parts.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet + a pencil/crayon. Optional: pattern blocks to build a house/rocket and then take it apart into its shapes.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: show the rocket — 'a triangle on top, a square for the body. That is 2 parts.'
2. GUIDED: do the house in Exercise 1 together — square walls + triangle roof.
3. YOU TRY: children draw the snowman's 3 circles (Ex 2), then Bit the robot's 4 parts (Ex 3).
4. Connect: 'Coders break a big job into small steps — just like we broke the robot into parts.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Ex 3 — Bit the robot = 4 parts (3 squares + 1 circle).

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: drawing the whole picture instead of separate parts — point to each empty box as one part.
Simplify: build the object with blocks, then lift each shape out and name it.
Extend: ask the child what other things are made of parts (a face, a flower, a car).
Movement option: build a 'robot' with bodies — children each become one part (head, body, feet).

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child draws the correct number of separate shape parts for each whole (2, 3, then 4).
